findings.text: Filter object holds two reference counters for shared lifetime and task usage, boolean markers for logging and killable receive waiting, an embedded decision cache, a link to the predecessor forming a stacked chain, a pointer to the compiled program, an optional notification context, a mutex guarding notification state, and a wait queue for interested pollers.
Fallback cache configuration carries no stored state. Its allow probe always declines the fast path and its preparation step performs no work, forcing full evaluation elsewhere.

Total compiled instruction budget along one evaluation path is bounded by a fixed byte allowance divided by the size of one classic filter record. Attachment accounting uses this bound to reject stacks that would exceed it.

Filtering snapshot is built from the current task register state, capturing the system call number, the architecture token, six argument words, and the instruction pointer. This snapshot is the sole input to cache checks and program runs.

Program loading validates classic filter code. Absolute word loads must be aligned and lie inside the snapshot size and are rewritten to an indexed form. Length queries are rewritten to the snapshot size as an immediate. Only an allowlist of return, arithmetic, load, store, move, and jump operations is accepted, and any other operation fails loading.

Fast allow testing first rejects numbers outside the bitmap length, hardens the index against speculation, then tests the corresponding bit. Architecture aware selection consults the native map for native snapshots and the compatibility map for compatibility snapshots where supported, while native only builds skip the architecture test. Unrecognized architectures emit a one time warning and decline.

Filter outcomes are ordered by their action field alone, ignoring attached data. Evaluation starts from an allow outcome, runs every filter along the predecessor chain, and keeps the least permissive action observed together with the filter that produced it.
When evaluation finds no filter where one is expected, it warns and forces process termination rather than permitting the call, preserving fail closed behavior on unexpected state.

Mode query and mode installation both require the caller signal lock to be held. Installation records the new mode before marking the task for filtering, with ordering enforced ahead of the atomic mark, and invokes architecture speculation mitigation unless the caller explicitly allowed speculative flaws.

Confinement mode starts disabled and may move to strict or filtering exactly once; an attempt to change from one active mode to a different one is rejected. Strict violations move the task to a dead state before termination. Thread synchronization may promote disabled peers to filtering but never demotes or switches active modes.
Empty predecessor denotes the universal root ancestor. Otherwise a candidate parent is an ancestor exactly when it appears anywhere along the child predecessor chain.

Eligibility scanning and thread synchronization both require the credential guard mutex and the signal lock to be held. Both skip the initiating thread and threads already exiting. Installation aborts without touching peers when group exit is already flagged, allowing a lockless check on release.

Synchronization is allowed only when every other live thread is either unconfined or already confined by an ancestor of the caller chain. Otherwise the numeric identifier of the first incompatible thread is returned, with an unresolvable identifier mapped to a missing process error accompanied by a warning. Zero indicates all peers are compatible.

Synchronization shares the caller head filter with each eligible peer with release publication, mirrors the caller filter count, propagates the no new privileges marker from caller to peer, releases the peer prior filter, and enables filtering on peers that were previously unconfined.

Preparation rejects empty programs and those beyond the classic instruction maximum, enforces that the caller either has no new privileges set or holds administrator capability in its user namespace, then allocates the filter object, initializes its notification lock and wait queue, compiles the program through the validator with conditional preservation of the original, and starts both reference counts at one.

User facing preparation copies a classic program descriptor from user memory, translating a 32 bit compatibility descriptor when invoked from a compatibility context, then delegates to internal preparation. Copy failure yields a fault error pointer.
Tracing probe calls on the native architecture are exempted from optimization analysis and treated as always allowed for caching purposes. All other numbers undergo full constant evaluation.

Cache construction interprets each candidate number with a restricted evaluator that understands only number and architecture loads, constant returns, unconditional and constant conditional branches, and constant masking. Any other load or operation disables caching for that number. The new map starts as a copy of the predecessor map or as all allowed when first, and bits are only cleared, never set, so the extended stack stays at least as restrictive.

Attachment totals the new program length plus each existing length with a small per filter penalty and rejects the stack when the sum would exceed the path bound. Caller flags may enable per filter logging, killable receive waiting, and synchronization across threads, with a variant controlling how unresolvable peers are reported.

Eight single bit selectors distinguish process kill, thread kill, trap, errno, trace, log, allow, and user notification outcomes. The default logged set enables every selector except allow, and administrative control may silence any action.

Trap, errno, trace, and user notification outcomes are logged only when both caller request and administrative enablement agree. Log and kill outcomes consult enablement alone, allow never logs, and process kill also serves as the default for unrecognized actions. When logging is selected, an audit record is emitted with the call number, signal, and action.

Strict confinement permits only a tiny fixed set of read, write, exit, and return primitives plus probe numbers where available, closed by a negative terminator, with a separate table selected for compatibility contexts. Any other number moves the task to dead state, records a kill log entry, and terminates with a kill signal.

Strict entry runs on each system call. It honors suspension under checkpoint restore with tracing, returns immediately when disabled, enforces the strict list when in strict mode, and faults on any other mode. A helper fetches the current call number, runs the same enforcement, then reports permission.

Architecture mitigation hook is weakly linked with a default that performs no action and may be overridden by architecture code. It is invoked when confinement is installed unless the caller explicitly permits speculative flaws.

Notification identifiers increment per filter with wrap permitted, uniqueness required only within the filter. Each request starts initialized, becomes visible after queueing, advances to sent once observed, and completes only after a reply. Descriptor additions are drained as they arrive and completed with install results, optionally resolving the request directly. Waiting uses interruptible sleep until the sent stage when killable waiting was requested, then killable sleep.

Identifier allocation and queue updates require the notification mutex. The wait loop holds the mutex while queueing and accounting, releases it while sleeping, and reacquires on wake to recheck state and drain descriptor work. Queueing increments the outstanding request count and wakes pollers, using a synchronous wake variant when so configured.

Visible notification code ends mid cleanup after interruption handling, so removal from the pending list, final error mapping, and return path beyond extraction of value and flags cannot be confirmed from this lane alone.

Evaluation reads the shared filter pointer once per call and treats absence as fatal. Installation publishes the new head with release ordering while elevating peers, and cache indexing hardens the bounded index before testing. Missing predecessor state and concurrent replacement therefore fail toward denial rather than permission.
